pairs.why: B's pink is a hotter magenta with a glow, while A's mid pink and warm cream-tan paper sit nearer the real card's softer pink and white-cream, though B's whiter cream edges also match the real card.
A has sandy-orange desert and muted blue sky with a black/red train, a restrained palette close to the real cards, while B's deep saturated blue sky and cool pale desert are pushed louder.
Both share the same lime-green rays, grey ground and white/orange/blue hues, so palette gives no reason to choose.
A's orange liquid is richer and its purple room is closer in chroma to the real card's saturated purple and orange, with a warm-cool contrast; B's duller glass reads more neutral.
B's umbrella has a red, yellow and orange mix on a cyan background, as on the real card, and its darker red underside gives richer shadow color than A's orange-heavy canopy.
A has the real card's neutral-light buttons against saturated blue and keeps a brighter yellow field, while B pushes everything into dark navy.
A keeps the real card's colors, including a yellow support and green slide with a pink wall. B turns the supports green and mutes the pink and tile, so it has fewer hue accents.
A's mid-green stripes and deep orange ring are closer to the real card's mid-green and saturated orange-red, while B's lime is yellower and louder.
